summary: The space $(\phi_C^{-1} \circ \mathcal{P})(H^{n-1}_{\mathrm{prim}}(X, \mathbb{R}))$ is a real subspace, but the basis elements $\sqrt{-1} [w_j]$ are purely imaginary under complex conjugation and do not lie in the real cohomology; the correct real basis requires $(y^i f_{j_i} - y^{n-1-i} \tilde{f}_{j_i}) / (2\sqrt{-1})$ rather than $\sqrt{-1} w_j$.

The numerator of $\mu$ is written as $\int_{\gamma_1} \omega \cdot \int_{\gamma_2} \omega - \int_{\gamma_2} \omega \cdot \int_{\gamma_1} \omega$, which identically vanishes because multiplication in $\mathbb{C}$ is commutative, missing the complex conjugation on the second factors.
